questions.idea: Demonstrate control evaluations and techniques in more complicated and realistic agentic situations.
questions.quote: We are excited about future work demonstrating these evaluations and techniques in more complicated and realistic situations.
questions.note: The founding paper asks for the toy-to-agentic transfer that Ctrl-Z (P004) and the SHADE-Arena protocol evaluation (P026) begin to deliver.

questions.idea: Analyze memoryful, history-dependent control protocols and their equilibria.
questions.quote: We leave the analysis of memoryful protocols, in which actions can depend on the full history of past observations, to future work.
questions.note: The adaptive macro-protocol of P003 is a first step toward history-dependent protocols.

questions.idea: Evaluate more red-team micro-strategies and macro-protocols robust to biased estimates.
questions.quote: While not exhaustive, our experiment provides a blueprint for future work evaluating more red team micro-strategies.
questions.note: Attack-selection work (P019, P020) shows the red team's strategy choice sharply lowers measured safety.

targets: new-axis:AI-assisted auditing with lower human reliability
questions.idea: Investigate AI-assisted auditing techniques that require less human involvement and lower reliability.
questions.quote: Future work needs to investigate AI-assisted auditing techniques that require less involvement and lower reliability from humans.
questions.note: No catalogued protocol yet reduces the human-auditor reliability the control frontier assumes.

targets: new-axis:deployment cost as a central optimization target
questions.idea: Take deployment cost into account as a central optimization target for control protocols.
questions.quote: We believe future work should consider taking cost into account as a more central optimization target.
questions.note: The control tax is measured but not yet optimized as the primary objective.

questions.idea: Expand the subversion-strategy methodology into a comprehensive benchmark.
questions.quote: We hope for a future work to expand on this methodology to create a comprehensive benchmark.
questions.note: SLEIGHT-Bench (P021) and MonitorBench (P041) extend the evaluation surface for subversion and monitoring.

questions.idea: Develop white-box methods that detect scheming via invariant activation patterns.
questions.quote: Whitebox methods remain a promising direction for future research: they could offer more direct and reliable ways to detect scheming if we can identify invariant patterns in model activations.
questions.note: Probe work (P043 negative results, P044 off-policy generalization) directly tests this white-box direction.

questions.idea: Build a comprehensive control safety case for internally deployed frontier LLM agents.
questions.quote: We hope this paper prompts discussion about what constitutes sufficient assurance against risks from internally deployed LLM agents.
questions.note: The CoT-monitoring roadmap (P036) and the trajectory framework (P006) develop the safety-case argument.

questions.idea: Quantify how communication-channel capacity translates into models' ability to coordinate attacks.
questions.quote: It remains an open question how the capacity of a given communication channel translates into the ability of models to coordinate attacks.
questions.note: Collusion studies (P022 focal points, P014 untrusted-monitoring safety case) address the coordination bound.

questions.idea: Incorporate stronger red-teaming and mitigate monitor vulnerabilities via ensembling or robust data routing.
questions.quote: These findings highlight the need for future work on control protocols to incorporate stronger red-teaming and to mitigate monitor vulnerabilities, either by monitor ensembling or by adopting robust data-routing mechanisms.
questions.note: Ensemble monitoring (P012) and TraceGuard (P015) are the ensembling / robust-routing responses.

questions.idea: Train models to write outputs legibly rather than only prompting for legibility.
questions.quote: Another area of future work is to train language models to write outputs legibly, instead of just prompting.
questions.note: Legibility is currently obtained by prompting; training for it is open.

questions.idea: Explore steganographic bandwidth in factored decompositions and blue-team measures to limit it.
questions.quote: Future research should explore what steganographic bandwidth can be achieved in decompositions in a Factor(U,U) protocol, and how blue-team measures for limiting that bandwidth trade off safety and usefulness.
questions.note: No catalogued paper measures the steganographic channel a factored protocol opens.

questions.idea: Test whether giving plan-monitors partial implementation context improves safety.
questions.quote: Future research should investigate whether changes to Factor(U,T), such as allowing monitors partial implementation context, can improve safety.
questions.note: Factor(U,T) (P011) opens the plan-monitoring direction it asks to extend.

questions.idea: Build monitors from architecturally diverse sources to test whether diversity yields robustness beyond prompt/fine-tune variation.
questions.quote: Future work is needed to build monitors from different sources to test whether architectural diversity yields robustness gains beyond what fine-tuning and prompting variation provide.
questions.note: The information-access study (P016) probes what makes a monitor detect sabotage.

questions.idea: Test monitor generalization to realistic deployments with ambiguous intent, longer horizons and distributed attacks.
questions.quote: How well these findings generalize to realistic deployments with ambiguous attacker intent, longer agent horizons, or attacks distributed across multiple episodes remains an open question.
questions.note: SHADE-Arena (P025) and Ctrl-Z (P004) supply longer-horizon realistic settings.

questions.idea: Develop robust elicitation methods for acausal collusion.
questions.quote: Developing robust elicitation methods for acausal collusion remains an open problem.
questions.note: Untrusted monitoring's trust rests on collusion elicitation that no catalogued method provides.

questions.idea: Evaluate whether monitoring dimensions generalize across ControlArena settings (infrastructure-as-code, APPS, vLLM).
questions.quote: Evaluating whether the same five monitoring dimensions generalize or require domain-specific adaptation across ControlArena settings is an important next step.
questions.note: Information-access work (P016) studies monitor generalization across settings.

questions.idea: Study how attacker trajectory length, serial-reasoning depth and main/side-task similarity affect monitor performance.
questions.quote: Future work should study how attacker trajectory length, the amount of serial reasoning required for the side task, and the similarity of main and side tasks affect monitor performance.
questions.note: An open direction the paper names but does not close.

targets: new-axis:learned attack selectors and adaptive blue-team responses
questions.idea: Develop learned (not prompted) attack selectors and blue-team protocols that adapt to selection.
questions.quote: Several directions remain for future work: learned (rather than prompted) selectors, blue-team protocols that adapt to selection, and deployment-level metrics that account for how the attack rate shifts under selection.
questions.note: No catalogued protocol yet adapts to a learned attack selector.

questions.idea: Continue enumerating monitor blind spots that uplift a monitoring red-teamer.
questions.quote: One important direction for future work is to continue enumerating monitor blind spots: conceptual insights that significantly uplift a monitoring red-teamer.
questions.note: A running catalog of monitor blind spots does not yet exist as a shared artifact.

questions.idea: Build more sophisticated sabotage evaluations, including a sandbagger that survives anti-refusal training.
questions.quote: We hope that the protocols and materials provided in this paper will serve as a starting point for future, more sophisticated evaluations of related capabilities.
questions.note: CTRL-ALT-DECEIT (P029) and Auditing Sabotage Bench (P027) extend sabotage evaluation.

questions.idea: Better elicit sabotage agents and monitors and use the suite as a pre-deployment dangerous-capability evaluation.
questions.quote: Our elicitation methods are far from exhaustive, and we hope that future work will better elicit sabotage agents and monitors.
questions.note: SHADE-Arena's own elicitation is acknowledged as non-exhaustive.

targets: new-axis:protocol variants raising usefulness at high safety
questions.idea: Explore protocol variants that increase usefulness while maintaining very high safety robustness.
questions.quote: We hope to see further variants of this strategy explored, in particular variants that increase usefulness while maintaining very high robustness on safety.
questions.note: The high-safety/high-usefulness corner of the frontier is not yet occupied.

questions.idea: Investigate whether CoT-monitoring effectiveness persists as model capability increases.
questions.quote: It remains an open question whether these CoT-monitoring trends will persist as model capabilities continue to increase.
questions.note: Reasoning-Under-Pressure (P039) shows training pressure already degrades monitorability.

questions.idea: Investigate CoT-monitoring in realistic coding environments with multi-step, distributed sabotage.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate monitoring effectiveness in more realistic coding environments where multi-step, distributed sabotage is possible.
questions.note: SHADE-Arena (P025) supplies the realistic multi-step sabotage setting.

targets: new-axis:detect and mitigate evaluation awareness in monitoring
questions.idea: Detect or mitigate evaluation awareness so CoT monitoring reflects genuine reasoning.
questions.quote: Future research should explore ways to detect or mitigate evaluation awareness, such as randomized test framing, so CoT monitoring reflects genuine reasoning rather than performative alignment.
questions.note: Evaluation awareness confounds every control measurement but has no dedicated mitigation here.

questions.idea: Build hybrid monitoring combining CoT analysis with behavioral and internal signals.
questions.quote: Future research should explore hybrid monitoring systems that combine CoT analysis with behavioral and internal model signals to maintain effectiveness under adversarial conditions.
questions.note: Probe negative results (P043) motivate fusing signals rather than trusting internals alone.

questions.idea: Turn 'models cannot achieve top-human stealth without being caught by a CoT monitor' into a safety case.
questions.quote: A safety case could argue that models cannot perform top-human-level stealth without being caught by a CoT monitor.
questions.note: The CoT-monitoring roadmap (P036) develops exactly this safety-case shape.

questions.idea: Invest in research on CoT monitorability alongside existing safety methods.
questions.quote: We recommend further research into CoT monitorability and investment in CoT monitoring alongside existing safety methods.
questions.note: MonitorBench (P041) and the faithfulness+verbosity measure (P037) operationalize monitorability.

questions.idea: Broaden alignment testing beyond safety-research sabotage.
questions.quote: We plan to broaden the scope of our alignment testing to cover areas aside from safety-research sabotage in the future.
questions.note: Gram (P031) generalizes sabotage-propensity auditing across tasks.

targets: new-axis:sabotage-propensity metrics not relying on chain-of-thought
questions.idea: Develop sabotage-propensity metrics that do not rely on the chain-of-thought.
questions.quote: Future work should develop improved evaluation metrics not relying on chain-of-thought.
questions.note: All current propensity readouts here lean on the CoT, which may itself be gamed.

questions.idea: Evaluate additional attack strategies to test generalizability across attack classes.
questions.quote: Future work should evaluate additional attack strategies to assess the generalizability of our findings across attack classes.
questions.note: Attack-selection work (P019) systematically varies the attack policy.

questions.idea: Can a fused behavioral + CoT + white-box monitor beat an adaptive attacker where each single channel fails?
questions.note: Across P006, P008 and P034 each single monitoring channel is shown evadable and P043 finds probes read the situation not the action; no catalogued paper builds and validates the fused monitor against an adaptive attacker.

questions.idea: What is the minimal shared context or channel under which untrusted monitors reliably collude, across single- and multi-agent settings?
questions.note: Synthesizes the focal-point collusion of P022 and the multi-agent SCHEME result of P023 into a channel-capacity question neither measures directly.

questions.idea: Does the protocol ranking (resample over defer over monitor) seen in toy/APPS settings hold in realistic multi-file agentic deployments, or invert?
questions.note: The head-to-head transfer implied by comparing P001/P002 (toy) with P004/P026 (agentic) is not measured directly anywhere in the catalog.

questions.idea: Do multilingual and training-pressure CoT degradation compound, so a capable model under RL pressure reasoning in a low-resource language becomes effectively unmonitorable?
questions.note: Combines the language-fragility failure (P042) and the training-pressure failure (P039) into a compounded worst case no paper has tested.

targets: region:RQ=RQ15;PROTOCOL=Trusted monitoring;THREAT=Covert side-objective;SETTING=Structured agentic sandbox;MONITOR=Trusted action monitor;GOAL=Measurement & modeling
questions.idea: Does specifying the forbidden behaviour abstractly ('do not subvert oversight') versus as concrete enumerated actions change the monitor's catch rate at equal usefulness?
questions.note: Red-gap-anchored: RQ15 (how to specify what the untrusted model must not do) is entirely uncovered in the catalog; this poses the experiment that would fill the authored specification gap.

questions.idea: Ensemble across auditors for deployment-time sabotage auditing.
questions.quote: Ensembling across auditors could be a promising direction for deployment.

questions.idea: Build monitors that are auditable, transparent and capable of structured intervention.
questions.quote: We encourage future work on monitors that are auditable, transparent, and capable of structured intervention rather than passive flagging.

questions.idea: Broaden alignment-sabotage testing beyond safety-research sabotage.
questions.quote: We plan to broaden the scope of our alignment testing to cover areas aside from safety research sabotage in the future.

questions.idea: Sabotage-auditing metrics that do not rely on chain-of-thought.
questions.quote: Future work should validate this assumption and develop improved evaluation metrics not relying on chain-of-thought.

questions.idea: Validate methods for preserving CoT monitorability.
questions.quote: We plan to pursue the project of Validating Methods for Preserving CoT Monitorability ourselves.

questions.idea: Study per-cue faithfulness differences and better elicitation of subtler misalignment modes.
questions.quote: Investigation of these per-cue dif- ferences in faithfulness and better elicitation of subtler mis- alignment modes is a fruitful area for future research.

questions.idea: Efficiently measure CoT monitorability.
questions.quote: Although monitorability provides a concrete alternative to faithfulness (Baker et al., 2025 ) , how to efficiently measure monitorability remains an open problem.

questions.idea: Effects of common incentives, adversarial and direct optimisation for monitorability across models and settings.
questions.quote: We hope that this work inspires further research into the effects of common incentives, adversarial optimisation, and direct optimisation for monitorability across more models and settings.

questions.idea: Probe CoT-monitorability information measures on negative-valued reward-hacking solutions via prompt hints.
questions.quote: For the BigMath environment, we encourage exploring the negative valued solution by providing hints in the system prompt, see Appendix C.3.2 .

questions.idea: Comprehensive benchmark basis for stress-testing and developing CoT monitors.
questions.quote: Overall, MonitorBench provides a basis for further research on evaluating future LLMs, studying advanced stress-test monitorability techniques, and developing new monitoring approaches.

questions.idea: Extend cross-language CoT-monitoring fragility tests to open-ended, multi-turn and tool-use settings.
questions.quote: This design supports precise measurement of hint-following and CoT deception, but future work can extend the framework to other datasets on open-ended generation, multi-turn dialogue, and tool-use settings.

questions.idea: Test sequence-level, nonlinear and cross-scenario probes for pre-action monitoring.
questions.quote: sequence-level probes, larger nonlinear classifiers, and probes trained directly across many tool-action scenarios remain open

questions.idea: Use distributional-distance measures to predict probe performance under distribution shift.
questions.quote: Further work could use distributional distance measures (Tong et al., 2021 ) to better characterise these gaps and predict probe performance under distribution shift, ideally with guarantees strong enough to inform deployment decisions.

questions.idea: Replicate and extend agentic-misalignment insider-threat evals with greater realism and better mitigations.
questions.quote: We hope others will attempt to replicate and extend this work, enhance its realism, and identify ways to improve current safety techniques to mitigate such alignment failures.

questions.idea: Use stealth evaluations to verify scheming inability under monitoring for a safety case.
questions.quote: We plan to use the stealth evaluations below for that future safety case as well, to verify scheming inability in the presence of monitoring.

questions.idea: Evaluate persuasion and deception dangerous capabilities across a wider range of settings.
questions.quote: The following are areas where we believe further research would be valuable: • For persuasion & deception, evaluating across a wider range of settings, e.g.

questions.idea: Run debates on harder questions and monitor whether obfuscated arguments become an obstacle.
questions.quote: Future work running debates on harder questions can monitor whether obfuscated arguments become an obstacle in practice.

questions.idea: Investigate harmfulness probes and other representation-reading methods.
questions.quote: Further investigation into Harmfulness Probes and other representation reading methods is left for future work.

questions.idea: Shift the trusted monitor from action evaluation to deception detection to extend its useful lifetime.
questions.quote: By shifting the role of the trusted monitor from action evaluation to deception detection, we hope to extend the useful lifetime of a trusted model even as frontier capabilities advance.

questions.idea: Use stronger experimental designs to resolve whether the honeypot null reflects robustness or weak attacks.
questions.quote: Whether this reflects genuine robustness or the limitations of our attack prompt remains an open question that stronger experimental designs can resolve.

questions.idea: Build settings where a model schemes despite its in-context goal aligning with the user.
questions.quote: Further research is needed to definitively categorize opus-3’s behaviors, and we encourage further research into settings where the model schemes despite the user’s objective and the model’s in- context goal aligning.

questions.idea: Collusion detection that adapts to varying agent counts and colluder/honest splits.
questions.quote: Future work could develop methods that adapt to varying N N and to arbitrary splits between colluding and honest agents, including the case where colluders outnumber honest ones.

questions.idea: Ensure efficacy of training-based elicitation and develop robust sandbagging-detection methods.
questions.quote: In the longer-term, further research is needed to ensure the efficacy of training-based elicitation, and develop robust methods for sandbagging detection.

questions.idea: Systematically evaluate anti-collusion interventions across diverse multi-agent environments.
questions.quote: Future work should systematically evaluate these interventions across diverse multi-agent AI environments, measuring both their effectiveness at reducing collusion and their impact on legitimate cooperation and system efficiency.

questions.idea: Improve linear deception probes via better training sets, SHIFT-controlled generalization and aggregation.
questions.quote: Future work could explore if improved training sets, controlling generalization with SHIFT (Marks et al., 2024), or different aggregation techniques improve performance.

questions.idea: Validate the oversight-game cooperative dynamics with real human overseers.
questions.quote: Validating these dynamics with real human overseers remains important future work.

questions.idea: Audit collusion in heterogeneous multi-agent deployments with varied models, permissions and tools.
questions.quote: Most experiments also use homogeneous teams with a shared model backbone, leaving heterogeneous deployments with varied models, prompts, permissions, and tool access for future work.

questions.idea: Head-to-head comparison of constraint-based steerability substrates for scalable oversight.
questions.quote: A systematic head-to-head is future work.

questions.idea: Extend constitutional deception-detection oversight to multi-agent environments.
questions.quote: Extending DeceptGuard to multi-agent environments is a high-priority future direction

questions.idea: Architectural requirements for control when the agent itself is the adversary.
questions.quote: This represents an open problem at the intersection of AI safety and computer security architecture.

questions.idea: Develop reliable misuse-safeguard evaluations that are not overly conservative.
questions.quote: Developing reliable evaluations without making them highly conservative is an important area for future work.

questions.idea: Evolve diverse red-team models for practical security-vulnerability detection.
questions.quote: provides a promising direction to solving practical security vulnerability detection problems in language models.

questions.idea: Whether reinforcing undetectable vs overt reward hacks differently affects alignment.
questions.quote: It is possible that reinforcing only undetectable reward hacks rather than overt reward hacks has different effects on alignment, but we leave this distinction for future work.

questions.idea: Test red-line risk with long-term, multi-agent, real-world deployment scenarios.
questions.quote: To robustly test red-line risk, future work should employ long-term, multi-agent, and real-world deployment scenarios for any model trending toward or exceeding this critical boundary.

questions.idea: Strengthen methods for evidencing trustworthiness in manipulation-attack safety cases.
questions.quote: Current methods for evidencing trustworthiness are largely insufficient and require substantial further research.

questions.idea: Determine whether AI agents coordinate secret collusion via common knowledge or weaker group knowledge, and develop detection strategies.
questions.quote: Note that it is an interesting open question whether in practice, generative AI agents coordinate rationally using common knowledge, and to what extent they rely on weaker concepts of group knowledge .
questions.note: P209 (tool-enabled undetectable steganography) and P212 (emergent stego collusion) partially address the coordination/detection question P211 formalizes.

questions.idea: Understand and mitigate the emergence of unintended steganographic communication in frontier LLM training.
questions.quote: This highlights the need for further research into understanding and mitigating the emergence of steganographic communication in LLMs.
questions.note: P209 shows realistic tool use already enables undetectable stego channels, sharpening the mitigation need P212 raises.

targets: new-axis:cryptographic shutdown backdoors and model self-awareness of them
questions.idea: Study whether models are self-aware of shutdown backdoors and whether cryptographic or mechanistically-inserted backdoors improve password-activated shutdown.
questions.quote: Future work could use cryptographic or mechanistically-inserted backdoors , and should study whether LMs exhibit self-awareness of shutdown backdoors .
questions.note: No catalogued protocol implements a cryptographic shutdown backdoor or tests a model's awareness of one.

questions.idea: Refine detection thresholds and metrics for execution-trace-consistency verification of untrusted code.
questions.quote: Future Research Directions Addressing these limitations requires a multi-pronged research agenda: Threshold calibration and metric refinement.
questions.note: CTVP's trace-consistency verifier needs the threshold calibration no catalogued monitor-hardening work yet provides.

questions.idea: Refine differential-auditing strategies per misalignment type and measure the information required for consistent hidden-behavior detection.
questions.quote: Our major contribution is the systematic exploration of this adversarial landscape under low-information constraints, establishing a foundation for future work refining strategies per misalignment type, developing robust approaches, and explicitly measuring information requirements for consistent model auditing in safety-critical applications.
questions.note: AuditBench (P216) supplies hidden-behavior model organisms against which to measure the detection information requirements P217 flags.

questions.idea: Evaluate the faithfulness and simulatability of long CoTs on complex/agentic tasks to derisk CoT monitoring.
questions.quote: In general, evaluating the faithfulness and simulatability of long CoTs on complex tasks remains an open challenge.
questions.note: The faithfulness+verbosity measure (P037) and MonitorBench (P041) operationalize the monitorability this asks to evaluate on harder tasks.

questions.idea: Test whether models can learn to evade latent-space monitors in ambiguous lie- and scheming-detection settings.
questions.quote: Studying whether models can evade latent-space monitors in ambiguous settings like detecting lies and/or scheming is a promising direction of future work.
questions.note: Strategic-deception probes (P058) and the pre-action probe negative results (P043) are the latent-space monitors whose robustness P219 questions.

questions.idea: Determine whether distribution shift lets advanced models sandbag the evaluations underpinning a scheming safety case.
questions.quote: Whether this distribution shift could lead to advanced models being able to sandbag such evaluations is an open question.
questions.note: Auditing games for sandbagging (P056) and CTRL-ALT-DECEIT (P029) probe exactly the sandbagging that could undermine an evaluation-based safety case.

questions.idea: Broaden alignment testing beyond research-sabotage to other misalignment areas.
questions.quote: We plan to broaden the scope of our alignment testing to cover areas aside from safety research sabotage in the future.
questions.note: Safety-research-sabotage evals (P030) and Gram (P031) begin broadening sabotage-propensity testing across tasks.

targets: new-axis:interaction effects of agent x environment scheming factors
questions.idea: Systematically test interaction effects between agent and environmental factors that drive scheming propensity.
questions.quote: Future work should systematically test for such interaction effects.
questions.note: P223's factor decomposition names the agent x environment interaction effects it does not yet measure.

questions.idea: Routinely report and improve evaluation realism to counter evaluation-awareness confounds in control measurements.
questions.quote: We advocate for routinely reporting evaluation realism alongside benchmark results, and will release our assessment tools to support this practice.
questions.note: The Honeypot protocol (P053) and LURE (P224) together attack the evaluation-awareness confound from the probing and realism-measurement sides.

questions.idea: Can a diverse monitor ensemble that scores cross-step temporal correlation, rather than per-step marginals, recover the detectability that P215’s marginal-preserving distributed-sabotage attack destroys for threshold and top-k monitors?
questions.note: Synthesizes the distributed detectability band (P215) with ensemble/diversity monitoring (P012): no catalogued monitor defends the correlation-encoded distributed attack P215 constructs.

questions.idea: Explore alternative audit architectures (automated scanners, HSM-backed trails, split-privilege) for agent control.
questions.quote: Future work should explore alternative audit architectures: non agent automated scanners, hardware security module backed audit trails, or split privilege models

questions.idea: Evaluate concealment and stable trigger behavior of temporal backdoors under sustained multi-step tool use.
questions.quote: Although a small number of samples in our dataset involved limited multi-step interactions, evaluating concealment and stable trigger behavior under sustained, multi-step tool use remains an important direction for future work.

questions.idea: Determine how tool-affordance safety findings generalize to other domains like healthcare or cybersecurity.
questions.quote: further work is required to determine how these findings generalize to other domains such as healthcare or cybersecurity.

questions.idea: Examine human-oversight challenges for agentic systems in resource-constrained settings.
questions.quote: Future work must examine oversight challenges and implications in resource-constrained settings.

questions.idea: Train deception probes that trigger only on the deceptive claim within an otherwise honest response.
questions.quote: We hope that probes can be trained which trigger only on the deceptive claim in the otherwise honest response.

questions.idea: Ensemble multiple specialized deception probes for comprehensive coverage.
questions.quote: Future work should explore ensemble methods combining multiple specialized probes for comprehensive coverage

questions.idea: Apply linear-representation deception techniques to backdoored and alignment-faking model organisms.
questions.quote: Future work applying these techniques to backdoored and alignment-faking models will be critical for bridging the gap to real-world alignment threats.

questions.idea: Test sandbagging-removal training when sabotage and honest failure are distinguished.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate whether our results hold when sabotage and honest failure are distinguished.

questions.idea: Standardized trajectory-level agent-safety benchmark (ATBench) for further sabotage evaluation.
questions.quote: to facilitate further research and standardized evaluation, we also introduced a challenging new benchmark, ATBench, for trajectory-level safety evaluation.

questions.idea: Whether voluntary collusion with secret tools transfers to open-ended real-world multi-agent deployments.
questions.quote: the extent to which voluntary collusion transfers to such settings is an empirical question

questions.idea: Empirically validate graduated human-oversight governance for AI-assisted engineering.
questions.quote: These remain analytical approximations ; empirical validation is future work.

questions.idea: Independently replicate scaffold-sensitivity of safety measurements with a pipeline built on a different model.
questions.quote: Subtler channels (prompt-format preferences, parse-rule tuning, answer-extraction heuristics) warrant independent replication with a pipeline built using a different model.

questions.idea: Use the extended-thinking stage to monitor misbehaviors like reward hacking despite CoT unfaithfulness.
questions.quote: While mitigating the unfaithfulness problem remains an open challenge, the extended thinking stage of LLMs presents a new opportunity to monitor model behavior, particularly misbehaviors such as reward hacking

questions.idea: Adaptive auditing policies that condition reasoning-faithfulness verification on uncertainty or task complexity.
questions.quote: Future work could explore adaptive auditing policies that condition verification on uncertainty or task complexity, enabling agents to dynamically trade off reasoning faithfulness and efficiency.

questions.idea: Study how post-training gives rise to strategic compliance (alignment faking).
questions.quote: We leave a detailed study of how post-training gives rise to strategic compliance to future work.

questions.idea: Extend the verifiable multi-agent evaluation framework across multiple domains and heterogeneous workflows.
questions.quote: Future work will extend domain-specific evaluation experiments to broader settings, testing AEMA across multiple domains and heterogeneous workflows.

questions.idea: Combine local-divergence streaming detection with LLM semantic checks for defence-in-depth deployment monitoring.
questions.quote: A production deployment combining both channels, local divergence for streaming detection plus LLM semantic check for high-stakes inputs, would provide defence in depth, though we leave this integration to future work.

questions.idea: Build on verified-code-generation to broaden avenues for agent-safety verification.
questions.quote: Building on the foundation of VeriGuard , several promising avenues for future research emerge.

questions.idea: Evaluate continual multi-agent conversation monitoring on naturalistic, weaker misalignment signals.
questions.quote: In future work, we plan to evaluate Arbiter on more naturalistic conversations with more diverse and weaker misalignment signals; for this reason, models of similar size to the arbiter will be used.

questions.idea: Formal verification tools certifying computational-graph equivalence to catch whitebox backdoors.
questions.quote: future work should focus on formal verification tools for computational graphs, capable of certifying functional equivalence before and after export.

questions.idea: Hybrid strategies to keep human oversight effort sub-linear in agent memory growth.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate hybrid strategies—active-learning prioritization, batched sampling with statistical guarantees, and tiered acceptance thresholds—to keep human oversight effort sub-linear in memory growth.

questions.idea: Adversarial reward auditing to build RLHF systems robust to novel exploitation strategies.
questions.quote: These findings suggest that adversarial auditing offers a promising direction for building RLHF systems robust to novel exploitation strategies.

questions.idea: Prove tighter theoretical results linking prover-estimator debate to realistic training methods.
questions.quote: future research can prove tighter theoretical results linking prover-estimator debate – or other, improved debate protocols – to realistic training methods.

questions.idea: Adapt emergent-misalignment datasets to RL to study backdoor/misalignment generalization.
questions.quote: Another vector of attack for future work is to adapt emergent misalignment datasets for use in reinforcement learning scenarios.

questions.idea: Develop a detection methodology for sleeper agents (identified as an open problem).
questions.quote: Critically, they provided no detection methodology, identifying this as an open problem.

questions.idea: Develop effective defenses against distributed multi-agent backdoor attacks.
questions.quote: The development of effective defenses against such attacks is an important area for further investigation and will be a key focus for future work.

questions.idea: Investigate temporal vulnerability patterns and defenses tailored to agentic execution.
questions.quote: Future research should investigate temporal vulnerability patterns, evaluate how traditional safety measures perform in agentic settings, and develop novel defense approaches tailored to agentic execution patterns.

questions.idea: Agency-prompt framing may make the model realize the task affects its future agency (an eval-awareness confound).
questions.quote: For agency prompts we encourage the model to be persistent, goal-directed and/or situationally aware (see Table 3 ), which could cause the model to realize that the current task impacts its future agency.

questions.idea: Develop control-based arguments within dynamic safety cases for frontier AI.
questions.quote: These patterns could be developed based on the frontier AI safety case sketches produced to date, and future work towards ‘control’ based arguments.

questions.idea: Study in-the-wild CoT unfaithfulness on datasets with multiple justifiable answers and real user query traces.
questions.quote: Future work should explore datasets with multiple justifiable answers to better reveal hidden biases in seemingly valid CoT rationalizations, and to apply our pipelines to real user query traces and other in-the-wild data.

questions.idea: Compare CoT-legibility across tasks and find post-training techniques that maintain legibility without cost.
questions.quote: Future work could directly compare the performance of models with varying degrees of CoT legibility on a broader range of tasks, investigate the specific post-training techniques that maintain legibility

questions.idea: Unify formal treatment of validate-then-act (TOCTOU) races across filesystem, browser-state and MCP settings.
questions.quote: Gap 3 calls for a unified formal treatment of validate-then-act races that covers both the filesystem and browser-state TOCTOU settings and the MCP tool-metadata setting under one model

questions.idea: Formal causal isolation of emergent strategic manipulation in multi-agent settings.
questions.quote: The post-hoc section should be read as a descriptive diagnostic layer that identifies where and how manipulation manifests, while leaving formal causal isolation to future work.

questions.idea: Measure self-replication risk when enterprise-grade controls are available.
questions.quote: Understanding how OR and AOC change when these enterprise-grade controls are available is valuable future work but represents a distinct research question beyond our current scope.

questions.idea: Synthesize runtime enforcement plans that provide formal guarantees of safe agent behavior.

questions.quote: Future directions: Future work should apply our framework to more realistic settings, such as RLHF, supervised fine-tuning, and AI control environments.

questions.quote: We plan to expand our evaluation framework to include additional LLM models, security challenges, and vulnerability categories.

questions.quote: Our findings call for further investigation into AI safety implications in autonomous multi-agent systems.

questions.quote: Generalization to other local LLM agent runtimes is left to future work.

questions.quote: There are already a number of techniques available to evidence inability arguments, though some of them are flawed and could be improved with further research.

questions.idea: Test whether faithfulness structural interventions scale to larger frontier models and longer-horizon agentic tasks.
questions.quote: Future work should test whether the same structural interventions scale to larger frontier models, longer-horizon agentic tasks, and settings where the shortcut is more subtle than explicit hint-following or lookup-table memorization.

questions.idea: Adaptive hyperparameters and richer frameworks that preserve reasoning-faithfulness transparency.
questions.quote: Future work should focus on adaptive hyperparameter strategies for smaller models, richer evaluation frameworks for reasoning faithfulness, and more efficient training methods that preserve transparency under resource constraints.

questions.quote: future work could extend validation to datasets such as SWE-bench

questions.quote: future work using LinuxArena to explore how richer control protocols, such as agentic monitoring and targeted sandboxing, can yield insights for the safe deployment of frontier agents.

questions.quote: there is substantial room for future work to construct sneakier attackers.

questions.idea: Whether agents spontaneously infer CoT monitoring and evade oversight without instruction.
questions.quote: can reasoning agents autonomously realize that their thoughts are being monitored and adapt their reasoning to evade oversight without any explicit instruction or optimization pressure to do so?

questions.quote: better elicitation with memory is future work.

questions.quote: Future work should test whether RL fine-tuning closes the gap, and should vary monitor capability to bound the regime where stego CoT becomes a deployment risk.

questions.idea: Whether self-obfuscation evasion arises organically from RL training paradigms.
questions.quote: Future research should explore whether similar evasive behaviors could arise organically from training paradigms like reinforcement learning, where a sophisticated reward model might implicitly penalize detectable internal states.

questions.quote: Improving our ability to make control evaluations in open ended, sometimes ambiguous, settings is an important direction of future work.

questions.idea: Move multi-agent safety cases from message monitoring toward information-flow assurance.
questions.quote: Long term, we hope this work helps move agentic AI safety from ad hoc message monitoring toward information-flow assurance for high-stakes multi-agent systems

questions.idea: Improve synthetic-data quality for black-box scheming monitors near their performance ceiling.
questions.quote: future work should focus on improving synthetic data quality.

questions.idea: Add severity-aware and ensemble monitoring so control protocols are not subverted by low-probability, high-severity attacks.
questions.quote: Recent developments in output monitoring, like the use of ensemble systems (Stickland et al., 2025) may improve safety.
questions.note: Ensemble monitoring (P012) and async ensembles (P195) are the diverse-signal monitors DrugBench points to for closing the probability-only monitor gap.

questions.idea: Teach a model to produce monitorable reasoning cues without modifying its weights, and cover richer reasoning behaviors.
questions.quote: future work may investigate methods for teaching a model to perform Behavior Cue Reasoning without needing to modify the original model's weights at all.
questions.note: Legibility protocols (P009) already push checkable outputs; Behavior Cue Reasoning asks to reach the same monitorability without weight edits.

questions.idea: Extend computer-use control evaluations across more platforms and realistic environments beyond Linux sandboxes.
questions.quote: In future work, we plan to extend CUAHarm to support other major platforms - such as Windows and Android - to more comprehensively evaluate CUAs across diverse real-world computing environments.
questions.note: LinuxArena (P189) and BashArena (P190) are the realistic system-level control settings CUAHarm's platform-coverage extension would broaden.

questions.idea: Use white-box residual-stream reading as an auditing tool that recovers reasoning even when behavioral CoT monitoring is blind.
questions.quote: Hidden computation that defeats behavioral CoT monitoring is, on these tasks, directly readable from the residual stream, suggesting monitorability is a property of the model's full computational trace, not just its surface tokens.
questions.note: Neural-Chameleons white-box evasion (P205) and WeightWatch weight-reading (P229) are the internals-based detectors this asks to pair with behavioral monitoring.

questions.idea: Lower monitoring overhead and extend graph-based multi-agent oversight to more complex, large-scale fault scenarios.
questions.quote: Future work will focus on optimizing the monitoring overhead and extending the framework to handle more complex fault scenarios in large-scale distributed systems.
questions.note: TraceGuard's multi-dimensional collusion-resistant monitoring (P015) is the direction SentinelAgent's large-scale graph oversight would scale toward.
